questions.question: What global extremum does $f(x) = x$ have on $\mathbb{R}$?
options: No global extremum
A global maximum only
A global minimum only
Both a global maximum and a global minimum

questions.question: What comparison defines a global maximum?
options: The value is at least as large as every value on the domain.
The value is at least as large as every nearby value.
The value is at least as large as the values at the endpoints.
The value is an upper bound that the function approaches.

questions.question: Why is attainment important in a global extremum?
options: The extremal value must be reached at a point in the domain.
The extremal value must be reached at exactly one point.
A supremum of the values suffices, even if never reached.
The extremal value must be reached at an interior point of the domain.

questions.question: For $f(x)=x^2$ on $[-1,2]$, where is the global maximum attained?
options: At $x=0$
At $x=1$
At $x=2$

questions.question: For the constant function $f(x)=1$ on $[0,1]$, where are global extrema attained?
options: At every point
Only at $x=0$
Only at the endpoints $0$ and $1$
At no point of $[0,1]$

questions.question: Why might a global extremum fail to exist on an open domain?
options: The limiting extreme value may not be attained in the domain
Continuous functions on open domains are unbounded
Open domains always make functions discontinuous
Open domains have no largest element, so $f$ has no largest value either

questions.question: How does a global extremum of $f$ on a domain $X$ differ from a local extremum?
options: It compares $f(x)$ only with values at inputs in a small neighbourhood.
It must occur at a point where $f'(x)=0$.
It compares $f(x)$ with the values at every input of $X$.
It is the most extreme of the interior local extrema.

questions.question: Let $f$ be defined on a closed interval $[a,b]$. Where can a global extremum of $f$ occur?
options: Only at interior points where $f'(x)=0$
Only at the endpoints $a$ and $b$
Only at points where $f$ is differentiable
At interior points or at the endpoints

questions.question: Let $f$ be defined on $X=\{1,2,3\}$ with $f(1)=4$, $f(2)=7$ and $f(3)=5$. What is the global minimum of $f$, and where is it attained?
options: Value $4$, attained at $x=1$
Value $1$, attained at $x=1$
Value $1$, attained at $x=4$
Value $7$, attained at $x=2$

questions.question: A continuous function $f$ is defined on a nonempty interval $X$. On which intervals can $f$ fail to attain a global maximum?
options: Only on unbounded intervals
Only on open intervals
On intervals that are unbounded or not closed
On no interval, since continuity guarantees a maximum

questions.question: Let $f(x)=x$ on the domain $X=(0,1)$. Which statement is correct?
options: $f$ attains no global extremum on $X$.
$f$ attains a global maximum at $x=1$.
$f$ attains a global minimum at $x=0$.
$f$ attains a global maximum at the point of $X$ closest to $1$.
